info.name: Greenhouse API
info.description:
Complete REST API for the Greenhouse Management Server.

## Quick start
1. Run **Auth / Login** — the JWT is automatically saved to `{{jwt}}`
2. All other requests use Bearer `{{jwt}}` via collection-level auth
3. Update `{{baseUrl}}` if your server runs on a different port

## MQTTX testing (simulate Arduino without a physical device)
1. Download MQTTX from https://mqttx.app/
2. Create a connection to your broker — by default `mqtt://localhost:1883`
3. **Subscribe** to `greenhouse/+/set/model` — you will see every model the server pushes to devices
4. Use **MQTT Debug / Publish (simulate Arduino telemetry)** from this collection to trigger a round-trip, OR publish manually from MQTTX to `greenhouse/<ip>/status` with the payload:
   ```json
   {"id":1,"zones":[{"id":1,"parameters":[{"id":5,"val":23.5}],"flowerpots":[{"id":1,"parameters":[{"id":10,"val":62.0}]}]}]}
   ```
5. After publishing, MQTTX will show the full model the server pushed back to `greenhouse/<ip>/set/model`

## Parameter field names (Arduino contract)
- `mutable` (not `mutableFlag`)
- `parameterType`: `"Toggle"` or `"Value"` (Arduino uses `equalsIgnoreCase("TOGGLE")`)

Returns a list of all greenhouses with their zones, parameters, status, and lastUpdate.

Manually push the full greenhouse model to the Arduino over MQTT (`greenhouse/<ip>/set/model`). Useful after changing configuration or when the device has re-connected.

`parameterType`: `VALUE` (numeric sensor reading) or `TOGGLE` (on/off actuator)
`mutable`: `true` means the Arduino can receive a `requestedValue` and act on it
TOGGLE type — the Arduino reads this with `parameterType.equalsIgnoreCase("TOGGLE")`. `requestedValue` of 1.0 = ON, 0.0 = OFF.

Update `requestedValue` for one or more parameters. After saving to DB, the server automatically pushes the **full** greenhouse model to the device over MQTT (`greenhouse/<ip>/set/model`).

Only `id` and `requestedValue` are required per item. Other fields in the body are ignored.

If you have MQTTX subscribed to `greenhouse/+/set/model`, you will see the push arrive within milliseconds.

item.name: MQTT Debug
item.description:
Endpoints for testing the server's MQTT integration without a physical Arduino.

## Round-trip test
1. Open MQTTX and subscribe to `greenhouse/+/set/model`
2. Send **Publish (simulate Arduino telemetry)** below
3. Watch MQTTX receive the full model the server pushes back

## Topic reference
| Direction       | Topic                             | Description                      |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Arduino → Server | `greenhouse/<ip>/status`         | Sensor telemetry (JSON)          |
| Server → Arduino | `greenhouse/<ip>/set/model`      | Full greenhouse model (JSON)     |
| Server → Arduino | `greenhouse/<ip>/set/config`     | Device config (triggers reboot)  |
| Server → Arduino | `greenhouse/<ip>/set/mapping`    | Sensor/actuator bindings         |

request.description:
Publish an arbitrary MQTT message via the server's broker connection.

The example body simulates a telemetry message from an Arduino at 192.168.1.100:
- Zone parameter ID 5: temperature = 23.5°C
- Flowerpot parameter ID 10: soil moisture = 62%

The server will receive this via its own `greenhouse/+/status` subscription, call `updateTelemetry()`, and push the full model back to `greenhouse/192.168.1.100/set/model`.

If the greenhouse was previously `NOT_RESPONSIVE` or `OFF`, its status will change to `ON` and the model push will happen automatically.

**Update the `id` values to match real IDs in your database.**

Simulates the first telemetry message from a device that was previously offline. The server detects the status was NOT_RESPONSIVE/OFF and pushes the full model so the device picks up any requestedValue changes that were made while it was offline.

Pre-condition: set the greenhouse status to NOT_RESPONSIVE first by calling GET /greenhouse/1 and checking it, or run `PATCH /greenhouse/1` to simulate it. Then send this request and watch MQTTX receive the model push.

Publish to any topic — useful for sending device config or mapping updates directly.

Change `topic` and `payload` to whatever you need. Remember to escape inner quotes in the payload string.

item.name: Analytics
item.description:
Retrieve parameter history charts, boot/crash event logs, aggregate stats, and manage analytics settings.

The folder pre-request script automatically sets `{{from}}` (24 h ago) and `{{to}}` (now) before every request. Override them on individual requests for longer ranges.

## Quick start
1. Run **Auth / Login** to get a JWT
2. Run **Seed test data** in the Analytics Dev folder to populate the DB
3. Use the requests below to query the data

exec: // Automatically set {{from}} and {{to}} to the last 24 hours.
// Override per-request if you need a different range.

request.description:
Returns up to `maxPoints` time-series readings for one parameter. Values are uniformly downsampled when the raw count exceeds `maxPoints`.

The folder pre-request script sets `{{from}}`/`{{to}}` to the last 24 h. Change `maxPoints` for higher/lower chart resolution.
Same as the 24 h request but the pre-request script overrides `{{from}}` to 7 days ago.
Same as the 24 h request but the pre-request script overrides `{{from}}` to 30 days ago.
Returns BOOT and CRASH lifecycle events for a greenhouse in descending order. Use `{{from}}`/`{{to}}` (set by the folder pre-request script) to control the time window.
Returns aggregate counts: `bootCount`, `crashCount`, and the queried `from`/`to` window.
Returns the singleton analytics settings row: enabled flag, retention periods, cleanup interval, and timestamp of the last cleanup run.

Updates analytics settings. `lastCleanup` is read-only and ignored if present in the body.

- `analyticsEnabled` — master switch; when `false` no new history or events are recorded
- `historyRetentionDays` — sensor readings older than this are deleted by the cleanup job
- `eventsRetentionDays` — boot/crash events older than this are deleted
- `cleanupIntervalHours` — how often the cleanup job runs (checked hourly, actual deletion only when interval has elapsed)
Convenience request — sets `analyticsEnabled` to `false`. No new data will be collected. Existing history and events are preserved and still queryable.

item.name: Analytics Dev / Seed
item.description:
⚠️ **Dev/test only** — remove or guard with `@Profile("dev")` before production.

Bypasses MQTT and the `analyticsEnabled` flag to write synthetic data directly into the database. Generated values oscillate smoothly within each parameter's configured `min`/`max` range.

## Typical workflow
1. **Seed all greenhouses** — generates 24 h of history + lifecycle events
2. Check results with the Analytics query requests
3. **Clear all data** — reset between test runs

item.name: Seed all greenhouses (24 h, 10 min interval)

request.description:
Seeds ALL greenhouses with 24 hours of parameter history (one reading per 10 minutes) and a realistic boot/crash event sequence.

Generated data:
- Sine-wave values bounded by each parameter's `min`/`max`
- ±4% random noise per point
- TOGGLE parameters alternate 0/1 every ~15 steps
- 1 BOOT event at the start + 1–3 CRASH/BOOT pairs spread across the window
- All values are deterministic for the same parameter/greenhouse ID

item.name: Seed all greenhouses (7 days, 30 min interval)

request.description: Seeds 7 days (168 h) of history at 30-minute resolution — good for testing the 7-day and 30-day chart ranges in the Flutter app.

item.name: Seed all greenhouses (1 h, 1 min interval — max resolution)

request.description: Seeds 1 hour of data at the maximum 1-minute resolution. Useful for testing downsampling behaviour and tooltip accuracy on zoomed-in charts.

item.name: Seed specific greenhouse (7 days, 30 min interval)

request.description: Seeds only the greenhouse identified by `{{greenhouseId}}`. Useful when you have multiple greenhouses and only want to populate one.

⚠️ Deletes ALL rows from `parameter_history` and `greenhouse_event`. Use this to reset the database between test runs.

Returns counts of deleted rows:
```json
{ "deletedHistoryRows": 864, "deletedEvents": 6 }
```

item.name: Configuration
item.description:
Push physical device config and sensor/actuator mappings to the Arduino.

All POST endpoints:
1. Save the config to the server DB (retrievable via GET)
2. Publish the JSON to the appropriate MQTT topic
3. Arduino saves to LittleFS and **reboots after ~2 seconds**

## Topic map
| Endpoint | MQTT topic | Arduino file |
|---|---|---|
| POST /config/devices | `greenhouse/<ip>/set/config` | `/config.json` |
| POST /config/mapping | `greenhouse/<ip>/set/mapping` | `/mapping.json` |

Network config (WiFi/MQTT broker) is intentionally not managed by the server — it must be provisioned directly on the device. Pushing credentials through the server creates a chicken-and-egg problem (device must already be connected to receive them) and risks storing passwords in plain text.

request.description: Returns the last device config (physical sensor/actuator hardware list) pushed to this device.

Saves and pushes the list of physical devices (sensors/actuators) to the Arduino.

Publishes to `greenhouse/<ip>/set/config`. Arduino saves to `/config.json` and **reboots**.

**Valid driver values:** `"analog"`, `"digital"`, `"DHT22"`, `"muxAnalog"`
**Valid type values:** `"value"`, `"toggle"`
Returns the last mapping config (sensor-to-parameter bindings) pushed to this device.

Saves and pushes sensor/actuator bindings to the Arduino.

Publishes to `greenhouse/<ip>/set/mapping`. Arduino saves to `/mapping.json` and **reboots**.

**paramName** must match the `name` field of a Parameter in the model exactly (case-sensitive).
**scope**: `"greenhouse"`, `"zone"`, `"flowerpot"`
**direction**: `"increase"` (e.g. heater warms toward target) or `"decrease"` (e.g. fan cools toward target)
**outputMode**: `"binary"` (on/off) or `"pwm"` (proportional)

For `muxAnalog` readDriver, `muxChannel` and `muxSelPins` (3-element array) are required.

Analog scaling: if `mapInMin != mapInMax`, the raw ADC value is linearly mapped to the physical range before updating `currentValue`.
